title: The Wild Swans
summary: A girl must craft magical items to free her brothers turned into swans.
coverScene: A young princess weaves shirts from green leaves while white swans fly near a stone castle.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a king lived in a great house with his dear children.
The older children were eleven brothers.
The youngest was a sweet little girl named Kizkardes.
They were very happy until a bad new head came into their lives.
The woman did not love the children.
She sent the young girl away to a farm.
The bad head also changed the eleven brothers into wild birds with a dark spell.
The big birds flew far away across the water into another country.
When Kizkardes grew older, she returned to the house to find her family.
She walked through a deep forest until she saw the beautiful birds near the sea.
The birds turned back into men when the sun went down behind the mountains.
They told her about the dark spell which could only be broken by a great work.
Kizkardes had to make eleven shirts from green plants that grew near the dark holes.
She could never speak a single word until every shirt was completely finished.
The strong girl began to pick the green leaves and work day and night without rest.
She sat in a quiet place and made the clothes with her own hands.
A young king found her during a hunting trip.
He brought her to his big house as his wife.
Even though she never spoke to him, the king loved her nice face very much.
Some bad people in the house told the king that his wife was a bad person.
They led her to a high public square because she would not answer their questions.
While the people watched from below, the strong girl held the green shirts in her hands.
Eleven wild birds flew down from the sky and stood around her on the ground.
Kizkardes threw the green shirts over the big birds just in time.
The spell broke, and the eleven brothers stood up as healthy young men again.
The youngest brother still had one bird part because his shirt lacked a hand cover.
The woman's dark plan failed completely.
The family lived happily ever after.
If she had not finished the work, the spell would have stayed forever.
Now the brothers have returned to their home.
They have lived together in peace since that day.
The king has understood the truth about his dear wife.
They have built a wonderful life in the great house.
Every person in the country has known their story well.
The young girl has shown great strength and love for her family.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a king lived in a great house with his dear children.
The oldest children were eleven brothers, and the youngest was a sweet little girl named Kizkardes.
They were very happy until a bad new leader came into their lives.
The leader did not love the children, and she sent the young girl away to a farm.
The terrible leader also changed the eleven brothers into wild birds with a dark spell.
The big birds flew far away across the water into another country.
When Kizkardes grew older, she returned to the house to find her family.
She walked through a deep forest until she saw the beautiful birds near the sea.
The birds turned back into men when the sun went down behind the mountains.
They told her about the severe spell which could only be broken by a great effort.
Kizkardes had to make eleven shirts from green plants that grew near the dark places.
She could never speak a single word until every shirt was completely finished.
The strong girl began to pick the green plants and work day and night without rest.
She sat in a quiet place and made the clothes with her own hands.
A young king found her during a hunting trip and brought her to his castle as his wife.
Even though she never spoke to him, the king loved her gentle face very much.
She worked very hard each day to finish the clothes for her brothers.
She sat by the window and picked the green plants until her hands were tired.
The king watched her from across the room and wondered about her silent life.
She never made any sound, but she always showed a kind smile to him.
Many people in the castle talked about her because she refused to speak.
However, the king protected her from all the bad words that other people said.
She continued to make the shirts because she loved her family so much.
Every single plant was important to the final success of her great task.
If she spoke just one word, her dear brothers would remain birds forever.
Therefore, she stayed quiet and kept working through the long hours of the night.
The green plants piled up around her chair as she worked without stopping.
She knew that her family depended entirely on her strength and focus.
The king often sat near her and tried to understand her quiet world.
He brought her food and water, but she only thanked him with her eyes.
The days passed quickly while she worked on the clothes in her small room.
She felt tired, but her heart remained strong because of her deep love.
The brothers flew near the castle every evening to check on her progress.
They watched her from the sky and hoped that she would succeed soon.
The time for the final test came closer with each passing week.
She gathered all the finished shirts and placed them carefully in a box.
Her fingers were tired from the work, but she felt happy and ready.
The plan was almost complete, and her family would soon be safe again.
She prepared herself for the final moment that would change everything.
Some bad people in the castle told the king that his wife was a bad person.
They led her to a high public square because she would not answer their questions.
While the people watched from below, the strong girl held the green shirts in her hands.
Eleven wild birds flew down from the sky and stood around her on the ground.
Kizkardes threw the green shirts over the big birds just in time.
The spell broke, and the eleven brothers stood up as healthy young men again.
The youngest brother still had one bird wing because his shirt lacked a part.
The leader's dark plan failed completely, and the family lived happily ever after.
The people in the square watched with great surprise as the birds became men.
The king ran forward and held his wife because he finally understood everything.
She looked at him and spoke her very first words with a happy smile.
The king was amazed to hear her voice for the very first time.
The brothers welcomed their sister and thanked her for her amazing strength.
The bad people who made trouble were driven away from the castle forever.
The king and his wife lived a wonderful life together with the eleven brothers.
The family stayed in the great house and never experienced any more trouble.
Everyone in the country celebrated the return of the strong young men.
The story of Kizkardes and her brothers became famous across the whole land.
People told the tale to their children for many years after that day.
The power of love and family had defeated the terrible dark spell.
Peace and joy returned to the country, and nothing could ever change it.

quiz.q: What happened to the eleven brothers because of the wicked queen?
options: They were changed into wild swans.
They were sent to a distant school.
They became kings of another country.

quiz.q: What rule did Kizkardes have to follow while making the shirts?
options: She could never speak a single word.
She had to finish them before the summer.
She was only allowed to work at night.

quiz.q: How did Kizkardes break the spell at the end of the story?
options: She threw the green shirts over the swans.
She spoke a magic word to the king.
She caught the birds in a large net.

sentences.text: In a sprawling estate of ancient stone and whispered memories, a benevolent monarch once lived surrounded by his cherished offspring.
The household numbered twelve in total, comprising eleven proud brothers and their youngest sibling, a gentle girl named Kizkardes.
Days drifted by in a golden haze of laughter and familial warmth until a severe, ambitious woman entered their domestic sphere.
Devoid of maternal affection or genuine warmth, the newcomer viewed the royal children with cold calculation.
She swiftly exiled the sweet young girl to a remote, desolate farm, severing her from the only life she had ever known.
Not content with mere banishment, the wicked stepmother cast a malicious spell upon the eleven brothers.
In the span of a single breath, they were transformed into majestic wild birds with midnight feathers and desperate hearts.
These bewildered creatures took flight, soaring across the vast expanse of the sea to seek refuge in an unfamiliar realm.
Years dissolved into memory, and as Kizkardes blossomed into resilient womanhood, an irresistible urge drew her back to her ancestral home.
She traversed a deep, impenetrable forest on foot until she reached the rocky coastline, where familiar silhouettes finally pierced the horizon.
As the sun dipped beneath the jagged mountain peaks, shedding its bruised gold light, the magnificent birds underwent a wondrous metamorphosis.
They shed their feathers and stepped forward as flesh-and-blood men, greeting their long-lost sister with tearful, trembling embraces.
Yet their reunion was shadowed by gravity, for the brothers revealed that a formidable enchantment bound them to their avian fate.
Only through an act of supreme sacrifice and immense physical endurance could the cruel spell ever be permanently shattered.
Kizkardes learned that she must weave eleven shirts entirely from stinging nettles gathered from dark, forgotten corners of the earth.
The instructions carried a heavy burden, demanding absolute silence from her lips until every single garment reached completion.
Should she utter even a solitary syllable, the formidable magic would instantly seal her brothers' fate as birds forever.
Without a moment of hesitation, the steadfast young woman began harvesting the rough, green plants despite the toll on her bare hands.
She established a secluded sanctuary where she worked tirelessly through the shifting hours of day and night.
Her dedication remained absolute, fueled solely by the desperate hope of restoring her family to their human forms.
Fate intervened one afternoon when a young king, tracking game through the quiet wilderness, stumbled upon her hidden refuge.
Captivated by her serene grace and the quiet dignity radiating from her features, he offered her a place within his castle.
She accepted his protection, though she maintained her strict vow of silence even as she crossed the threshold of her new home.
The king grew deeply enamored of her gentle demeanor, often lingering in her chambers just to bask in her peaceful presence.
Although he found her wordless existence profoundly mysterious, his growing affection insulated her from the rising tide of courtly gossip.
Envious courtiers whispered malicious speculations through the corridors, questioning the strange silence of the king's new bride.
Yet the king stood resolutely between his wife and the petty detractors, shielding her with his unwavering trust and authority.
Meanwhile, Kizkardes remained utterly focused on her arduous labor, sitting by the tall window as daylight waned into dusk.
Her fingers grew calloused and bruised from working the stiff, prickly nettles into soft, wearable cloth.
The green shirts accumulated slowly around her wooden chair, each finished seam representing a prayer for her displaced brothers.
Every evening, the eleven brothers soared above the castle battlements, circling the high towers to check upon her grueling progress.
Their silent vigilance offered her quiet comfort as she labored through the lonely hours while the rest of the citadel slept.
The king often observed her from across the chamber, bringing trays of food and fresh water with tender concern.
Unable to speak words of gratitude, Kizkardes would only thank him with the eloquent appreciation shining in her eyes.
Weeks bled into months, and the climax of her long ordeal approached with the inexorable steady march of time.
At last, the final shirt was completed, and she carefully packed the woven garments into a sturdy wooden chest.
Her hands throbbed with fatigue, but a profound sense of triumph warmed her chest as she prepared for the final test.
Dark forces within the castle, however, made one last desperate attempt to turn the king's affection into doubt and fear.
Conspiring courtiers convinced the monarch that his mute wife practiced illicit magic, pointing to her secretive habits as proof.
Trapped by circumstance and unable to defend herself with spoken words, she was led toward a high public square for judgment.
A vast crowd gathered beneath the stone platform, whispering and pointing fingers at the pale yet resolute young woman.
Kizkardes stood calm amid the hostile murmurs, clutching the bundle of green shirts tightly against her chest.
Just as the officials prepared to condemn her, a rushing sound filled the air as eleven wild birds descended from the heavy clouds.
They landed in a protective circle around her, beating their dark wings against the stone to keep the hostile crowd at bay.
With a swift and practiced motion, Kizkardes stepped forward and threw the green shirts over the majestic creatures.
In an instant, the fierce enchantment shattered like fragile glass, and the eleven birds transformed back into healthy, grown men.
Only the youngest brother retained a single feathered wing upon his left shoulder because his shirt had lacked a sleeve.
The wicked stepmother's grand design collapsed completely, rendering her malicious efforts entirely and permanently void.
Gasps of astonishment swept through the assembled crowd as the miraculous transformation unfolded before their eyes.
Realizing the truth at last, the king rushed past the guards and pulled his bewildered, brave wife into a tight embrace.
Looking into his bewildered eyes, Kizkardes parted her lips and spoke her very first words with a radiant smile.
The king stood frozen in utter amazement, hearing the sweet music of her voice for the very first time in his life.
The eleven brothers crowded around their sister, offering tearful thanks for the unimaginable strength that saved them.
The treacherous courtiers who had sown discord were swiftly driven from the castle gates, never to return.
Peace and deep joy finally settled over the land, sealing a legendary tale of familial devotion that would echo through the ages.

quiz.q: What specific item did Kizkardes need to weave to break the spell?
options: Eleven shirts made from green plants
A single royal cloak made of silk
Eleven blankets made from forest wool

quiz.q: Why did the youngest brother retain a bird wing after the spell was broken?
options: Because he refused to wear the shirt she made
Because his shirt was missing a sleeve
Because he was too far away from the crowd

quiz.q: What condition was placed upon Kizkardes while she worked on the task?
options: She had to live outside the castle walls
She could never speak a single word
She was forbidden from seeing her brothers
